title: Microsoft Purview role groups: who can run which compliance and data governance tasks?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the permissions, licensing, expiry limits and administrative-unit controls. Three routes omit the intervening pages used when editing custom role groups; these are minor navigation omissions, not incorrect controls.

claims.claim: A Microsoft Purview role group is a named set of roles.
claims.quote: A role group is a set of roles that enable users to do their jobs across compliance and governance solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Adding a member grants the effective permissions of the roles assigned to the group.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: A role grants permission to perform a set of tasks.
claims.quote: A role grants permissions to perform a set of tasks.

claims.claim: Case Management lets users work with eDiscovery cases.
claims.quote: For example, the Case Management role lets users work with eDiscovery cases.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal uses RBAC.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview portal uses the role-based access control (RBAC) permissions model.

claims.claim: Most Microsoft 365 services use RBAC.
claims.quote: Most Microsoft 365 services use RBAC, so if you're familiar with the permission structure in these services, granting permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal is similar.

claims.where: What it is: Built-in role groups
claims.claim: The portal includes default role groups for the tasks and functions of its compliance and governance solutions.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview portal includes default role groups for tasks and functions for each compliance and governance solution that you need to assign people to.

claims.quote: Insider Risk Management | Use this role group to manage insider risk management for your organization in a single group.

claims.where: What it is: Built-in role groups
claims.claim: Microsoft generally advises adding individual users to default role groups as needed.
claims.quote: Generally, add individual users as members to the default role groups as needed.

claims.where: What it is: Built-in role groups

claims.claim: Administrators can create custom role groups.

claims.where: What it is: Custom role groups

claims.where: What it is: Custom role groups
claims.claim: Administrators can later change a custom role group's description.
claims.quote: On Name the role group, update the description for the custom role group in the Description field.

claims.where: What it is: Custom role groups

claims.where: What it is: Custom role groups
claims.claim: Administrators can later change a custom role group's members.
claims.quote: You can also select any of the currently assigned users and groups and select Remove members to remove the users or groups from the role group.

claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Portal security-group membership is supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organisations.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Assignment options
claims.claim: A user or security-group role group assignment can have an expiry date.

claims.claim: Role group members can be assigned to one or more administrative units.
claims.quote: On Assign admin units, select the check box for all the administrative units you want to assign to the users or groups.

claims.claim: Administrative units subdivide the directory in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: By using administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID, you can subdivide your organization into smaller units and restrict administrative permissions to specific parts of your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.claim: Role Management allows viewing, creating and modifying role groups and is the role required by the documented portal procedures.
claims.quote: The Role Management role allows users to view, create, and modify role groups.

claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role

claims.where: What it is: Who manages them
claims.claim: Global Administrators can create and modify role groups through Organization Management permissions.
claims.quote: Global admins are automatically added as members of this role group

claims.where: What it is: Who manages them

claims.quote: Role Management | Manage role group membership and create or delete custom role groups. | Organization Management  Purview Administrators

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph

claims.quote: The roles that appear in the Microsoft Entra ID section of the Roles and scopes area are Microsoft Entra roles

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph
claims.claim: Compliance Administrator is shown as an Entra role mapped to the Purview Compliance Administrator role group.
claims.quote: Compliance Administrator | Help your organization stay compliant with any regulatory requirements, manage eDiscovery cases, and maintain data governance policies across Microsoft 365 locations, identities, and apps. | Compliance Administrator

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph

claims.quote: Security Reader | View and investigate active threats to your Microsoft 365 users, devices, and content, but (unlike the Security operator) they don't have permissions to respond by taking action. | Security Reader

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Entra roles shown in Roles and scopes are managed in Microsoft Entra rather than Purview.
claims.quote: To manage members of a Microsoft Entra role, select Manage members in Microsoft Entra ID. This choice redirects you to the Azure management portal.

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph
claims.claim: Permissions managed through Purview role groups cover compliance and governance features available within the Purview portal, not every service-specific permission.
claims.quote: Managing permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal only gives users access to the compliance and governance features that are available within the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: What it is: Entra roles paragraph
claims.claim: Exchange mail flow rule permissions are granted in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To grant permissions to other features that aren't in the Microsoft Purview portal, such as Exchange mail flow rules (also known as transport rules), use the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Role groups govern access to alerts.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management Analysts | Use this group to assign permissions to users that act as insider risk case analysts. Users in this role group can access all insider risk management alerts, cases, and notices templates.

claims.claim: Role groups govern content preview access.
claims.quote: Preview | View a list of items that are returned from content searches, and open each item from the list to view its contents.

claims.claim: Role groups govern investigation access.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management Investigators | Use this group to assign permissions to users that act as insider risk data investigators.

claims.claim: Role groups govern policy configuration access.
claims.quote: Users in this role group can create, read, update, and delete insider risk management policies, global settings, and role group assignments.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends roles with the fewest permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends that you use roles with the fewest permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Entra roles override scoping; controls[4].note
claims.claim: An overlapping Entra role takes precedence over administrative-unit scoping on a Purview role assignment.
claims.quote: When both scoped Microsoft Purview role assignments and Entra roles are present, Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.

claims.claim: Expiry is optional and configured per assignment.
claims.quote: Automatic expiring permissions are optional and are configured on a per-user assignment basis.

claims.claim: An assignment without an expiry is permanent until removed.
claims.quote: Administrators can create temporary assignments with an expiration date, update an existing expiration date, extend an assignment, or remove the expiration to make the assignment permanent.

claims.claim: Administrative-unit scoping is optional, and an unscoped assignment permits organisation-wide access.
claims.quote: If administrators don't have administrative units assigned (unrestricted administrators), they can assign policies to the entire directory without being required to select individual administrative units.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate charge for creating or assigning Purview role groups.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview role groups creating assigning separate price charge licensing. Opened purview-permissions and the Microsoft Purview service description on learn.microsoft.com; neither documents a separate role-group creation or assignment charge.

claims.claim: Any user benefiting from the Microsoft Purview service requires a licence.
claims.quote: Any user benefiting from the service requires a license.

claims.claim: Users assigned a Purview role for use in the portal are an example of users benefiting from the service.
claims.quote: Users with a Purview role assigned for use in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview service description provides solution-specific licensing requirements.
claims.quote: For more information about licensing options for Microsoft Purview features, see the Microsoft Purview service description.

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 is one of the qualifying Purview subscriptions for administrative units.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Purview licensing (one of the following subscriptions):

Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5

All built-in and custom role groups except the following support automatic expiring permissions:

claims.where: Risks and limits: Expiry does not cover every group; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Expiry periods range from a minimum of one day to a maximum of two years.
claims.quote: A minimum expiration period of one day and maximum expiration period of two years can be selected from the current date in the local time zone of the administrator who sets the expiration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Expiry is silent
claims.claim: No notification is sent before temporary permissions expire.
claims.quote: You don't receive a notification before permissions expire

claims.where: Risks and limits: Expiry is silent
claims.claim: No additional audit record is generated when temporary permissions expire.
claims.quote: nor are any additional audit logs are generated when a user's temporary permissions expires.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Expiry is silent
claims.claim: Role assignment expiry does not affect actions already in progress.
claims.quote: Actions that are already completed or in progress aren't affected, but any new operation is denied after the assignment expires.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overlapping assignments keep access
claims.claim: Individual and security-group assignments of the same role group retain independent expiry dates.
claims.quote: If a user receives the same role group through both an individual assignment and a security group assignment, each assignment retains its own expiration date.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overlapping assignments keep access
claims.claim: Access persists while either overlapping assignment remains valid.
claims.quote: Access remains active as long as one of the assignments is still valid.

claims.where: controls[5]; Risks and limits: Direct assignments have no just-in-time activation
claims.claim: There is no documented just-in-time activation control for direct user assignments to Purview role groups.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview role groups direct user assignment just in time activation PIM. Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions and read Purview Role Assignment Migrator search excerpts; direct assignments have no activation control.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits: Direct assignments have no just-in-time activation
claims.claim: Just-in-time role-group access works through security groups using PIM for Groups.

claims.claim: Assignment expiry is set under Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > user or group > Edit expiration.

claims.fix: Keep the printed route for built-in groups. Add to the row's note: 'For custom groups: Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Name the role group > Edit roles of the role group > Edit members of the role group > user or group > Edit expiration.' The intervening wizard pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a PowerShell or API control for expiry on Purview role-group assignments.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview role group assignment expiration date PowerShell API Set-RoleGroupMember; "Purview" "role group" "expiration" "PowerShell" "API". Opened Learn purview-permissions and Add-, Update-, Set-RoleGroup references; no assignment-expiry parameter or endpoint.

claims.claim: Assignment scoping is set under Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > user or group > Assign admin units.
claims.quote: To update the administrative units for users or groups, select any of the currently assigned user or groups and select Assign admin units.
claims.fix: Keep the printed route for built-in groups. Add to the row's note: 'For custom groups: Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Name the role group > Edit roles of the role group > Edit members of the role group > user or group > Assign admin units.' The intervening wizard pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented PowerShell or API assignment of administrative-unit scope to Purview role-group members.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview role group member administrative unit scope PowerShell API Assign admin units; "Purview" "administrative units" "PowerShell" "role". Read Learn purview-admin-units, purview-permissions, Add-RoleGroupMember and Update-RoleGroupMember; no such operation.
